newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Ikarus, Russia ZiL to build buses jointly.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Ikarus, Russia ZiL to build buses jointly.

text.p: Hungarian busmaker Ikarus Jarmugyarto Rt said on Tuesday it planned to join forces with Russian truckmaker AMO ZiL to start producing as many as 7,000 buses a year in Moscow from 1997.
"We plan to start shipping 5,000-to-7,000 partly-built buses for final assembly at a ZiL factory in Moscow," Ikarus president Gabor Szeles told Reuters.

"We started talks with ZiL two months ago, and I hope we can create a joint venture by mid-January so production can start in February," Szeles added, noting the initial investment from both companies would total "a few million dollars."
The venture would start by assembling Ikarus mid-range buses and minibuses, but cooperation could expand to include Ikarus production of ZiL trucks in Hungary, he said.
"Demand for buses in Moscow is huge, but some of our output there also could be exported to central Europe," Szeles said.

Ikarus and ZiL, the biggest busmaker and truckmaker respectively in the old East bloc during communism, hope the venture will help reverse steep drops in their production since the collapse of their main market, the former Soviet Union, in 1991.

ZiL, which built nearly 230,000 trucks at its peak in 1988, made barely 15,000 units in 1995. Similarly, Ikarus built over 13,000 buses at its height in 1986, but its output is expected to reach only 800 units in 1996.
